subject: Private deployment — customer keys, support access & subprocessor questions
messages:
From: Karan Patel <kpatel@stellarus.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Vogt <lena.vogt@stellarus.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:07:00 -0500
Subject: Clarifying key control and support access for private deployment

Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week — Stellarus is excited about the Private deployment option. Before we proceed to procurement we need clarity on a few privacy and security points so we can sign the DPA and complete our internal review:

- Customer-managed keys: can you confirm the options for bringing our own KMS (Cloud HSM / AWS KMS)?
- Support access: in an emergency does Redwood ever require temporary access to decrypted data for troubleshooting? If so, what's the process and what controls/logs are in place?
- Subprocessors: please provide an up-to-date list and your notification cadence for new subprocessors.
- Cross-border flows: our data residency team needs to know whether any telemetry, logs, or metadata from a VPC-deployed tenant would transit outside the EU.

If you can send a short summary and any DPA redlines we can review, that would help unblock legal/infosec.

Thanks,
Karan
Procurement Lead — Stellarus

[Attachment: none]
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Karan Patel <kpatel@stellarus.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarifying key control and support access for private deployment

Karan — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front and I've attached the DPA redline + subprocessors list and a KMS flow diagram for VPC/on-prem options.

- Customer-managed KMS: Supported. For VPC we support AWS KMS customer-owned keys (Bring Your Own Key) and you can configure an external HSM for on-prem. The runtime never stores plaintext keys; we accept wrapped keys or KMS aliases per the runbook.
- Support access: Redwood does not require routine access to plaintext customer data. Emergency troubleshooting is handled via an ephemeral access model: temporary, logged support sessions using customer-approved jumpbox credentials and an auditable justification ticket. No decryption is performed without customer consent except in a court-ordered scenario — we'll require a narrow, time-limited agreement.
- Subprocessors: attached CSV lists current subprocessors and their roles. We notify customers via the console and by email 30 days before onboarding new subprocessors, and you can opt into immediate notification for security-critical subprocessors.
- Cross-border flows: For Private VPC-deployed tenants, control plane metadata (billing/usage aggregates and error traces) may be stored in Redwood's control plane in the US; customer data payloads and KV caches remain in-customer VPC or on-prem unless you opt into managed backups. We can arrange EU-only control plane for enterprise customers under Private.

Next steps: Evelyn (legal) is cc'd and can respond on the DPA redlines. Aditya — can you validate the KMS diagram and add any operational constraints? I'd like to propose a 30-min runbook call Wed or Thu next week.

Thanks,
Mina
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: RWI-DPA-v3_redline.pdf, subprocessors_manifest_202611.csv, kms_keyflow_vpc_onprem.png
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Karan Patel <kpatel@stellarus.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Clarifying key control and support access for private deployment

Karan / team — quick technical clarifications on the options Mina outlined:

- VPC (managed by customer): The inference runtime (containers + caches) runs in your VPC. Keys live in your AWS KMS; Redwood's agents are configured to call your KMS endpoint with no key material ever leaving your environment. For emergency troubleshooting we use an out-of-band support workflow: a temporary role you grant with time-limited STS tokens and all actions require an approval ticket. We record CloudTrail entries on both sides.

- On-prem package: You keep the entire stack. Redwood provides signed binaries and an operator guide. Support access is via customer-managed VPN and SSH jumpbox; we do not receive keys or any persistent access unless you explicitly provision them.

- Ephemeral decryption: In the unlikely event we need to reproduce an issue requiring plaintext, we prefer reproducible tests with mock data or you can grant an ephemeral key via the KMS "GenerateDataKey" pattern; the key is returned wrapped and destroyed after the session. All sessions captured in audit logs.

- Subprocessor list summary: Only a small set of subprocessors handle telemetry (SaaS monitoring, crash reporting). No subprocessors have access to raw model inputs/outputs for Private VPC unless you authorize managed backups. We also support contractual commitments for subprocessors in Appendix B of the DPA (see attachment).

Happy to run through the runbook with your infra/security team. Proposed times: Thu 10:00-10:30 CET or Fri 15:00 CET.

—Aditya
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: support_escalation_playbook.docx]
From: Lena Vogt <lena.vogt@stellarus.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karan Patel <kpatel@stellarus.ai>, legal@stellarus.ai
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 08:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Clarifying key control and support access for private deployment

Mina,

Thanks for the detailed response and attachments. A few follow-ups from our legal & data protection teams after reviewing the redline:

1) Subprocessor notification: we need a contractual obligation that Redwood will provide at least 45 days' notice and an option for us to object to a new subprocessor on reasonable grounds. Please confirm.

2) Control plane residency: if you offer EU-only control plane as an option, can you confirm the SLA and availability of EU-only telemetry ingestion? Our regulator requires EU residency for metadata associated with EU customers.

3) Support and decryption: we need an explicit clause that Redwood support personnel will have no direct access to plaintext model inputs/outputs unless we provide an ephemeral key, and that such sessions must be recorded and require approval by an identified Stellarus admin.

4) SCCs / transfers: provide the mechanism for lawful transfer (SCCs or adequacy decision) if control plane telemetry is processed in the US.

We'll prepare a tracked-redline and send it back; for now please confirm (1) and (3) in writing so procurement can proceed in parallel.

Best,
Lena
Legal Counsel — Stellarus

[Attachment: Stellarus_DPA_comments.docx]
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Vogt <lena.vogt@stellarus.ai>, Karan Patel <kpatel@stellarus.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 05 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarifying key control and support access for private deployment

Lena / Karan — thanks for the comments. Summary & commitments from Redwood legal below (we'll incorporate into the DPA redline):

- Subprocessor notification: we can commit to 45 days' prior notice and include an objection mechanism with reasonable-cause criteria in the DPA. If an objection is raised we will pause onboarding until it's resolved or provide mitigation measures.

- Support/decryption: Redwood confirms support personnel will not have direct access to plaintext model inputs/outputs without an explicit customer action to provide an ephemeral key. Any ephemeral access will require:
  * Prior written approval from the customer's designated admin
  * A formal ticket with justification
  * Time-limited credentials and one-time use keys
  * Full session recording and audit trail retained for 1 year (or adjustable per contract)

- EU-only control plane: We offer an EU control plane option for Private deployments. We'll include an SLA addendum covering availability and data residency; aditya & diego will provide the operational playbook during the runbook call.

- SCCs / transfers: We'll provide standard SCCs for transfers and can support a Data Transfer Addendum if required.

Next steps: attached is a brief DPA summary (RWI-DPA-v3_redline.pdf). I'll open a DocuSign envelope with the DPA + Data Transfer Addendum and KMS checklist. Please review and confirm a time for the runbook session — Aditya proposed Thu 10:00 CET; we can do that if it works for your infra team.

Evelyn Hart
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
